purpose: Test whether attack onset can be forecast from attack-free network-flow history on completely held-out IoT devices using a device-agnostic network representation.
claim_scope: cross-device clean-onset forecasting development pilot; attack labels are not held out by family in V35
final_validation: locked; no existing Garuda final-validation family is scored by V35

device_split.selection_rule: lexicographic device-id partition frozen before model results; no label or metric information used

temporal_protocol.history_rule: all eight history minute bins must exist and must not overlap any annotated attack interval
temporal_protocol.positive: one or more annotated attack onsets occur after the cutoff and within 240 seconds
temporal_protocol.negative: the next four observed minute bins exist and do not overlap an annotated attack interval and contain no attack onset
temporal_protocol.split_unit: entire device; a device exists in exactly one split

feature_policy.history_representation: per-history robust median/IQR normalization followed by last, mean, std, max, delta, recent-2-minus-prior-2 and recent-4-minus-prior-4 summaries

models.primary: HistGradientBoostingClassifier with fixed hyperparameters and class_weight=balanced
models.calibration: logit logistic calibration on calibration-device samples only
models.threshold: 95th percentile of policy-device benign calibrated scores; policy FPR budget 5%

claim_boundary: A pass would support cross-device prediction of attack onset in this UNSW development corpus from clean network histories. It would not prove unseen-family zero-day prediction, compromise prediction, or universal attack forecasting.
